description.narrative: SONGO project is implemented in 18 unions of 6 UPZs in Kurigram and Gaibandha district under Rangpur division. The details about beneficiaries are as follows: Household-112000, Women with Reproductive Age (WRA)-95000, Male Adult-90000, Adolescents-80000

To improve maternal and child nutrition through effective upazila level nutrition governance mechanisms in operation, improved maternal and child health practices, improved WASH and hygiene practices, and improved household access to nutritious food.

Two districts of Rangpur Division Gaibandha and Kurigram are the most disaster-prone area and a good number of land of these districts are in the riverine side and char land. The people of these area are to face flood or other natural disasters each and every year as a result they are to count a good amount of loss, outbreak of diarrhea and other diseases are found, scarcity of safe drinking water are also found, crops and WASH structures are damaged and finally livelihoods are greatly hampered. As a result the nutritional status are poor of these areas compared to the other districts. SONGO has been working with the people of riverine side and char land of this areas to improve maternal and child nutrition through strengthening local nutrition governance mechanisms in operation, improved maternal and child health practices, improved WASH and hygiene practices, and improved household access to nutritious food covering the multi-stakeholder planforms since 2018.

title.narrative: Number of people with improved food security

description.narrative: Number of households with an improved score on the household food insecurity access scale (HFIAS) compared to the baseline score. This score is a household score and needs to be translated to the number of individual household members (based on average household size)

title.narrative: Number of women with diversified diets

description.narrative: Individual dietary diversity scores aim to reflect nutrient adequacy. Studies in different age groups have shown that an increase in individual dietary diversity score is related to increased nutrient adequacy of the diet. Dietary diversity scores have been validated for several age/sex groups as proxy measures for macro and/ or micronutrient adequacy of the diet. Number of women with an improved dietary diversity, as shown by an improved score on the Minimum Dietary Diversity for Women (MDD-W) compared to the baseline. It can be used as a proxy indicator for nutrition adequacy and quality of food for the whole household by multiplying the number of women with scoring in a certain category with the average or actual household size.

title.narrative: Number of households with diversified diets

description.narrative: Number of households with an improved dietary diversity, as shown by an improved score on the Household Dietary Diversity score (HDD) compared to the baseline. The household dietary diversity score (HDDS) is meant to reflect, in a snapshot form, the economic ability of a household to access a variety of foods. Studies have shown that an increase in dietary diversity is associated with socio-economic status and household food security (household energy availability) (Hoddinot and Yohannes, 2002; Hatloy et al., 2000). If assessment of the nutrient adequacy of the diet is of primary concern, it is best to collect information at the level of the individual by means of the Minium Dietary Diversity for Women (MDD-W).
